title: Canonical strict-local map in closed affine quotient charts
statement: Let $i:Z\to W$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], let $\bar a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], with underlying point $a\in Z$, and choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W$ containing $i(a)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion]. Write $i^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, let $\mathfrak p\supset I$ be the prime of $i(a)$, put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=(A/I)_{\mathfrak p/I}=R/IR$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $K\subset\Omega$ be the separable algebraic closure of the common residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Put $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{W,i\bar a}$ and $D=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Z,\bar a}$, the coordinate rings of the strict localizations of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with structural maps $j_W,j_Z$. Let $u:C\to D$ be the canonical local ring homomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3), so that $j_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}u=i\circ j_Z$. Then $j_W$ and $j_Z$ factor through $U$ and $i^{-1}(U)$, respectively; their chart maps give local structure maps $R\to C$ and $S\to D$ for which $C$ and $D$ are algebraic strict henselizations relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Both rings are strictly henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and their geometric evaluations identify their residue fields with $K$, with structure maps induced by $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\subset K$. The map $u$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism, with $D$ viewed as an $R$-algebra through $R\to S$, and induces $\mathrm{id}_K$ on residue fields. In particular $u(IC)=0$. For $Q=C/IC$ and its quotient map $q:C\to Q$, equip $Q$ with the induced $S=R/IR$-algebra structure. There is a unique $S$-algebra map $\bar u:Q\to D$ with $u=\bar u\circ q$; it is local, and $\bar u^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)=q(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_Q$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-strict-local-closed-chart-models] to obtain the two individual chart models, their pointed presentations and specified residue identifications.

The structural square of the uniquely pointed canonical strict-local map, the two chart factorization equations and the pullback square imply equality after composing with j. Cancel the open immersion j and apply faithfulness of Spec to obtain u alpha = beta quotient. Localization extensionality then gives u composed with R to C = R to S to D. The pointed equation characterizing the canonical map gives epsilonD u = epsilonC by Spec faithfulness. Substitute the chart-model evaluation equations and cancel the embedding K into Omega to obtain presentationD.residueMap u = presentationC.residueMap. If u(c) is a unit, its residue in K is nonzero, so c has nonzero residue and is a unit. Thus u is local.

For a in I the chart equation gives u(alpha(a))=beta(0)=0. The map/comap adjunction for ideals gives IC contained in ker(u). Set Q=C/IC and q the quotient map; define v:Q to D by the quotient lift of u. The composite R to C to Q kills IR because it sends a in I to q(alpha(a))=0. Its quotient lift defines the actual S-algebra structure on Q. The R-algebra equation for u and surjectivity of R to S prove that v respects this S-action. Surjectivity of q proves uniqueness of the resulting S-algebra homomorphism.

The ring map v:Q to D makes Q nontrivial. A nontrivial quotient of the local ring C is local. If v(q(c)) is a unit then u(c) is a unit; locality of u makes c a unit, hence q(c) is a unit. This proves locality of v. The image of the maximal ideal under the surjective quotient map q is the maximal ideal of Q. Locality of v identifies its maximal-ideal inverse image with that ideal, giving both required equalities.
